newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rates rise on central bank squaring.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rates rise on central bank squaring.

text.p: Mexico's Cetes rates rose in line with expectations at the primary treasury bill auction on Tuesday as Mexican banks sought to square their monthly positions with the central bank, analysts said.
On Tuesday, the bellwether one-month rate rose 65 basis points to 18.35 percent, well within expectations. A rise in U.S. long bond yields also pushed up rates, analysts said.
A survey of nine Cetes dealers by Reuters earlier in the day found expectations of a rise of 75 basis points in the one-month paper.
"What we saw in the auction was the same thing that causes pressures every month due to the squaring of positions," said ING Barings economist Sergio Martin.
"Investors start to cover their positions so not to pay (a penalty to the central bank). For me the problem is a passing one and rates will probably keep falling in the next few weeks," Martin said.
Mexican banks are forced to balance their shortfalls with the central bank each month, and that can cause a scramble for funds in the secondary market.
That in turn can cause primary rates to rise at Banco de Mexico's weekly primary auction.
Rates were kept from rising higher this week by optimism in Mexican financial markets in general, while Mexico's weak inflationary background has continued to keep players happy, analysts added.
A Reuter survey of 14 brokerages and research firms in Mexico found expectations of a rise of 0.88 percent in the consumer price index for July. That inflation number will be released on Thursday.
"Inflation is expected to come out in line with expectations and there will likely be no surprises," said Fernando Alcantara, director of the money market for Finamex.
Rates also rose across the yield curve this week. The rate on the 91-day paper rose by 18 basis points to 19.18 percent.
The 181-day paper yielded 20.39 percent compared to 20.25 percent last week. One-year paper yielded 20.52 percent compared to 20.24 percent last week.
Demand rose slightly as well, coming in at 11.11 billion pesos compared with 10.31 billion pesos last week.
Cetes have been a good bet recently.
Mexico was the best performer in J.P. Morgan's Emerging Local Markets Index, posting a 3.66 percent increase due to its continued fundamental improvement, the company said in a release.
